subject: korean
title: Too late for the pool?
goal: Combine a notice and a friend's message to judge whether the planned arrival time works, name the lines that decide it, and write a reply that gives the real deadline.
thinking: Combining two sources
Finding which rules decide the case
Giving a reason, not only a verdict
differsFromPlain: Plain practice reads one clock time or says when a class starts. Here a rule inside the notice (what happens after the start) changes the answer, and you must find it and tell the friend the real deadline.
prerequisites: Can read Hangul and clock times written with 시 and 분
Knows 오후, weekday names and basic -아요/어요 endings
material:
Today is 수요일. A notice is on the door of the swimming pool, and your friend 민지 sends you a message.

[수영 수업 안내]
- 수업: 화요일, 목요일 오후 4시 30분 ~ 5시 30분
- 수업 시작 10분 전까지 수영장 앞으로 오세요.
- 수업이 시작되면 문을 닫아요. 늦으면 들어갈 수 없어요.

민지: 내일 수영 수업 4시 40분까지 가면 돼요?

steps.prompt: Can 민지 go at 4시 40분 tomorrow? Decide using the notice.

options.text: Yes. The class lasts until 5:30, so she can still join.
options.reveals: You used the end of the class. Look for what the notice says happens once the class has started.

options.text: Yes, if she tells the teacher that she will be late.
options.reveals: You assumed there is a way to enter late. Look for what the notice says about arriving late.

options.text: Cannot tell: the notice has no time for tomorrow.
options.reveals: Today is 수요일, so tomorrow is 목요일, and the notice does list 목요일.

options.text: No. The door closes when the class starts at 4:30.
options.reveals: You linked the start time with the door rule and checked 4:40 against both.

steps.explain: Tomorrow is 목요일, so there is a class at 4:30. The door closes when it starts, and the notice asks people to come 10 minutes earlier (4:20). 4:40 is after both times.
hints: First work out which day tomorrow is, then find that day in the notice.
Put 4시 40분 next to the start time and next to the line about the door.

steps.prompt: Which facts from the notice prove that 4시 40분 is too late? Choose all that you need.

options.reveals: This is a basic fact: it is the time that 4:40 must be compared with.
The end time says when the class is over, but not when people can no longer enter.

options.text: People should arrive 10 minutes before the start.
options.reveals: This gives a safe arrival time, which is stricter than the start time.

options.text: There are classes on 화요일 and 목요일.
options.reveals: This shows that a class exists tomorrow, but not whether 4:40 is late.

options.text: The door closes once the class has started.
options.reveals: This is the rule that turns a late arrival into a closed door.

steps.explain: The start time (4:30), the door rule and the 10-minute request together show that 4:40 is too late. The end time and the days do not decide it.
hints: Ask of each fact: does it help me compare 4:40 with a limit?
Facts that only tell you a class exists, or when it ends, do not set a limit for arriving.

acceptable.reason: The start time and the door rule already settle the case; the 10-minute line only adds the recommended earlier time.

steps.prompt: Reply to 민지 in Korean (polite -요). Tell her the latest time she should arrive and give the reason from the notice.

checks.label: names the arrival limit (4시 20분 or 10분 전)
gives a reason (late / door closed / start)

selfAssess: Does my reply tell 민지 one clear time?
Does my reason come from the notice (door closes, start time)?
Would 민지 know what to do tomorrow?

modelAnswers.text: 아니요, 4시 20분까지 가야 해요. 4시 40분은 늦어서 들어갈 수 없어요.
modelAnswers.note: Says no, gives the limit and the reason.

modelAnswers.text: 수업 10분 전인 4시 20분까지 오세요. 수업이 시작되면 문을 닫아요.
modelAnswers.note: Gives the limit by explaining the notice.

badAnswers.why: Accepts the wrong time and gives no reason.
Gives a vague reason but no time.

steps.humanReview: Whether the Korean is natural and whether the limit and the reason really match the notice.
hints: Start with 아니요 or 안 돼요, because the plan does not work.
Write the time with 시 and 분, then add a short reason with 서 or 니까.

rubric.full: Uses the day, the start time and the door rule to reach 'no' and names the deciding facts
rubric.partial: Reaches 'no' but without naming the deciding facts
rubric.none: Says yes or gives no reason

rubric.full: Gives the 4:20 limit (or 10 minutes before) with a reason in polite Korean
rubric.partial: Says it is too late but gives no clear time

alternatives: Telling 민지 to arrive 'by 4시 15분' or 'around 4시' is also fine, as long as it is before 4:20.
A student may say 'no' only because 4:40 is after 4:30; that is already correct, the 10-minute line is extra.
hardCases: A reply that says 4시 30분 before without mentioning the 10-minute request: it is not wrong against the door rule but is looser than the notice; a teacher decides.

cautions.language: 시 (o'clock) and 시간 (length of time) are easy to mix up; the checks only accept digits or spoken forms followed by 시/분. 'Late' is 늦다: 늦으면 = if (she is) late.
cautions.culture: Community pools and centers in Korea often close the door at the start of a class; this notice states the rule, so no cultural knowledge is assumed.
cautions.accessibility: All times are written out with 시 and 분 (not 4:30), so screen readers read them in Korean. The notice is a plain text list; no images or colors carry meaning.

auto: Choice of the verdict and of the deciding facts
Presence of the time limit, a polite ending and a reason in the reply
human: Quality and naturalness of the reply

subject: korean
title: The wrong floor
goal: Compare a text message with a floor guide, find the line that sends someone to the wrong place, and rewrite it correctly in matching casual speech.
thinking: Checking a message against a notice line by line
Spotting a detail that does not match
Repairing the line while keeping the register
differsFromPlain: Plain practice asks which floor a place is on. Here the guide is right, a friend's message mixes in one wrong detail, and you must notice it and fix the sentence.
prerequisites: Can read Hangul and floor numbers written like 3층
Knows that casual speech to a younger sibling can drop 요
material:
Your classmate 지우 is explaining to her younger brother 하나 how to find the library. First read the floor guide on the library door, then check 지우's text message.

[도서관 안내]
1층: 안내 데스크, 카페
2층: 어린이 책방
3층: 열람실 (조용히 공부하는 곳)
4층: 강당 (행사가 있을 때만 열어요)
엘리베이터: 1층 입구 왼쪽

steps.prompt: One line of 지우's text would send 하나 to the wrong place. Which line is it?
lines: 도서관에 가면 먼저 1층 안내 데스크로 와.
steps.explain: Line 3 is wrong: in the guide the 열람실 is on the 3층, while the 2층 is the children's bookroom. The other lines match the guide (안내 데스크 on 1층, elevator at the left of the entrance).
hints: Compare the lines one at a time with the matching entry in the guide.
Check the floor number and what the guide says is on that floor.

steps.prompt: Rewrite line 3 so that 하나 goes to the right floor. Keep casual speech (반말) like 지우's other lines.
selfAssess: Does my sentence say the correct floor for the 열람실?
Does it still sound like talking to a younger brother?
Is it a complete sentence?

modelAnswers.text: 공부하는 열람실은 3층에 있어.
modelAnswers.note: Direct fix of the wrong number.

modelAnswers.text: 열람실은 3층이야. 엘리베이터 타고 올라와.
modelAnswers.note: Fixes the floor and adds a helpful action.

badAnswers.why: Repeats the wrong floor.
Right floor, but the stiff ending does not fit a message to a little brother.

steps.humanReview: Whether the casual register is natural and the sentence is complete.
hints: Find 열람실 in the guide and read its floor.
Keep the ending like 있어 or 이야, not 있습니다.

rubric.full: Picks the line that contradicts the guide
rubric.partial: Picks a nearby line
rubric.none: Picks a line that matches the guide

rubric.full: Right floor, 열람실 named, casual ending kept
rubric.partial: Right floor but the register or the place name is lost

alternatives: Writing 3층 as 삼층 or '세 번째 층' is acceptable.
A fix that also mentions the elevator is fine.
hardCases: A student may think line 4 is wrong because the elevator is not mentioned by floor; the guide only gives its position, so it is correct.

cautions.language: Floor numbers use Sino-Korean numbers + 층 (3층 is 삼층, said 'sam-cheung'); the casual endings -어 / -이야 are for close friends or younger people.
cautions.culture: Libraries in Korea often put a children's room on a lower floor and a quiet study room higher up; the guide states this, so no knowledge is assumed.
cautions.accessibility: The guide is a plain text list. Floor numbers are written as digits + 층 so a screen reader reads them in Korean.

auto: Which line is picked; presence of 열람실, 3층 and the casual ending

subject: korean
title: Which question do I need?
goal: Decide which pieces of information are missing before you can answer an invitation, and ask for them in a short polite message.
thinking: Seeing what is already known and what is missing
Choosing questions that settle the decision
Asking politely in Korean
differsFromPlain: Plain practice answers an invitation with yes or no. Here you cannot answer yet; you decide which unknowns matter for your own schedule and ask only those.
prerequisites: Can read Hangul and times written with 시
Knows polite -아요/어요 endings and question forms like 몇 시에 ...?
material:
Today is Friday. This is your plan for Sunday, and then a message from your friend 수아.

[내 일요일 계획]
- 오전 10시 ~ 11시: 가족 산책
- 오후 6시: 할머니 댁에서 가족 저녁 식사

수아: 일요일 오후에 영화 볼래요? 영화관 앞에서 만나요.

steps.prompt: You want to say yes if you can still be on time for dinner. Which questions do you NEED to ask 수아 first? Choose all that apply.

options.reveals: A start time is handy for planning, but your only fixed event is dinner at 6, so the end of the film matters more.
This is about the film, not about your time.
You looked for the moment you are free again.
You thought about getting from the cinema to the dinner, which also takes time.
Price is a different kind of question from time.

steps.explain: Your only fixed event in the afternoon is dinner at 6. To decide, you need the time the film ends and how far the cinema is from where you must be. The film's cast or the price do not change your time.
hints: List what you already know about Sunday afternoon, then list what is still unknown.
Ask of each question: could its answer make me late for 6 o'clock?

acceptable.reason: The end time alone settles it if the cinema is close to the dinner place.
Asking for both start and end time gives the length of the film, a reasonable extra.
Start, end and place together give a complete picture, although the start time is not strictly needed.

steps.prompt: Write a short polite reply (-요) to 수아: say that you want to go, mention what you have in the evening, and ask for the information you need.

checks.label: asks for the end time or the place

selfAssess: Do I say what limits me (dinner at 6)?
Does my question ask for something that decides my answer?
Is the message short and polite?

modelAnswers.text: 가고 싶어요! 그런데 6시에 가족 저녁이 있어요. 영화가 몇 시에 끝나요?
modelAnswers.note: Wants to go, names the limit, asks for the end time.

modelAnswers.text: 좋아요. 저녁에 할머니 댁에 가야 해서요. 영화관이 어디에 있어요?
modelAnswers.note: Gives the reason and asks for the place.

badAnswers.why: Says yes without checking the dinner and asks nothing.
Asks a question, but not about what limits the evening, and gives no reason.

steps.humanReview: Whether the questions are natural and really tied to the evening plan.
hints: Start with a short yes-wish, then say what you have at 6.
End with one question that uses 끝나요 or 어디에 있어요.

rubric.full: Picks the end time and the place (or defends the end time alone)
rubric.partial: Picks one needed item plus an unnecessary one

rubric.full: Polite message that states the limit and asks a deciding question
rubric.partial: Asks a question but does not state the limit, or the reverse

alternatives: Asking only for the end time is reasonable if the student assumes the cinema is near.
A student may ask 'how long is the film?' (영화가 몇 시간이에요?); this is also a good question.
hardCases: Whether the start time is 'needed': if the start time is unknown the end cannot be guessed, so a student who asks for it is not wrong.

cautions.language: 몇 시에 = at what time; 끝나요 = it ends. -ㄹ래요 and -ㄹ까요 are both used to invite; here -ㄹ래요 is the friend's invitation.
cautions.culture: Sunday family meals at a grandparent's home are common in Korea but not universal; the plan only sets a time limit and does not depend on the custom.
cautions.accessibility: Times are written with 시, no calendar table or image. The questions are full Korean sentences, so a screen reader reads them as text.

auto: Which questions are chosen; polite ending, limit mention and question form in the reply
human: Whether the questions are natural and relevant

subject: korean
title: Book the room
goal: Combine room rules from a notice with a teammate's message and find several different booking plans that satisfy every condition.
thinking: Turning text conditions into limits
Finding several solutions under constraints
Testing a plan against every rule
differsFromPlain: Plain practice asks for one time from a timetable. Here several rules and a teammate's limit apply together, many plans work, and you must find three different ones.
prerequisites: Can read hour times written with 시 and the words 부터 and 까지
Can compare clock hours
material:
Your team wants to use the after-school room. Read the notice and the message from your teammate 서준.

[방과 후 교실 이용 안내]
- 이용 시간: 오후 1시 ~ 6시
- 한 번에 1시간이나 2시간 쓸 수 있어요.
- 오후 3시 ~ 4시는 청소 시간이라 쓸 수 없어요.

서준: 저는 수업이 2시에 끝나서 2시 전에는 갈 수 없어요. 시작 시간은 정각으로 해 주세요.

steps.prompt: Warm-up: 서준 suggests using the room from 오후 2시 to 4시. Why does this plan fail?

options.text: It runs into the cleaning time.
options.reveals: You compared the whole time span of the plan, not only its start, with the cleaning hour.

options.text: It starts before 서준 is free.
options.reveals: 서준 is free from 2 o'clock, so check the start against his message again.

options.text: It lasts longer than the room allows.
options.reveals: Two hours is allowed; count the hours again.

options.text: It ends after the room closes.
options.reveals: The room is open until 6 o'clock, so check the end time again.

steps.explain: 2시 ~ 4시 includes 3시 ~ 4시, when the room is being cleaned. Every plan must be checked for its whole time span, not just for its start.
hints: Write the start hour and the end hour of the plan.
Compare the plan's hours with each line of the notice.

steps.prompt: Find 3 different booking plans that follow the notice and 서준's message. s = start (오후 s시), h = hours you use the room.

constraints.fail: Use a whole hour for the start and for the length.
The room can be used for 1 hour or 2 hours at a time.
서준 cannot come before 2 o'clock (and the room opens at 1).
The room is open only until 6 o'clock.

constraints.ok: Does not touch the cleaning time.
constraints.fail: Your plan overlaps the cleaning time (3시 ~ 4시).

steps.explain: Four plans work: 오후 2시~3시, 4시~5시, 4시~6시 and 5시~6시. A plan fails if it starts before 2, runs past 6, uses 3 hours, or touches 3시~4시.
hints: Write each rule as a limit on the start hour or on the end hour.
Try a start hour, add 1 or 2 hours, and check the end hour against the cleaning time.
After you find a plan, change only the length and check it again.

because.prompt: Pick ONE of your plans and send 서준 a short message in Korean saying when you will use the room.

checks.label: says from when / until when or how long

selfAssess: Do the times in my message match one plan that works?
Does my plan avoid 3시 ~ 4시?

modelAnswers.text: 4시부터 6시까지 방과 후 교실을 써요.
modelAnswers.note: A two-hour plan after the cleaning.

modelAnswers.text: 2시부터 3시까지 한 시간 쓰는 건 어때요?
modelAnswers.note: A one-hour plan before the cleaning; asks politely.

badAnswers.why: Agrees but names no time.
Only a length, no clock time and no polite ending.

because.humanReview: Whether the times in the message really match a valid plan (the check only finds that a clock time is present).
hints: Use one start time and one end time from your list.
Use ~부터 ~까지 to say from when until when.

rubric.full: Finds three different plans that satisfy every rule
rubric.partial: Finds one or two valid plans
rubric.none: Plans break rules (cleaning time, 2 o'clock, 6 o'clock)

rubric.full: Polite message with times of one valid plan
rubric.partial: Message with a time that does not match a valid plan

alternatives: Any three of the four valid plans are fine.
A student may give the plan as '2시 ~ 3시' in Korean words only; the message check allows that.
hardCases: A plan that ends exactly at 3시 or starts exactly at 4시 may look like it touches the cleaning time; it does not.

cautions.language: ~부터 ~까지 = from ... until ...; 정각 = exactly on the hour; 'hour' as a point is 시 and as a length is 시간.
cautions.culture: After-school rooms and sign-up rules are typical for Korean schools but the notice explains all rules.
cautions.accessibility: All conditions are given as text with hour numbers; the build step uses two number fields and no image.

auto: Whether each plan satisfies every rule, and that the three plans differ
human: Naturalness of the message and its match with the chosen plan

subject: korean
title: Where is 유나?
goal: Locate a friend from clues that arrive one at a time and change your answer when a new notice changes what a clue means.
thinking: Using a clue as evidence
Updating a guess when new information arrives
Noticing that a clue can stop being unique
differsFromPlain: Plain practice asks where a shop is on a map. Here the clues come one by one, and a later notice changes what an earlier clue proves.
prerequisites: Can read place words such as 정문, 후문, 편의점, 은행, 꽃집
Knows how to read a short text message
material:
You are going to meet your friend 유나 near school, but you cannot see her. This is the map on the school notice board, and then 유나 sends messages one by one.

[학교 주변 안내]
정문 앞: 편의점, 은행
후문 앞: 편의점, 꽃집
공원 앞: 카페

steps.prompt: Decide where 유나 is after each new clue.
hints: Compare each clue with the shops on the map.
Ask whether the clue appears at only one place.

stages.ask: Where do you think 유나 is?

options.reveals: A guess that rests on one shop which also exists at the other gate.
A guess that rests on one shop which also exists at the other gate.

options.text: I need one more clue before I can say.
options.reveals: You noticed that the clue fits two places.

stages.after: Both gates have a 편의점, so this clue fits two places. Any of these answers is reasonable if you stay ready to change it.

stages.ask: Where do you think 유나 is now?

options.reveals: On the map, the 후문 has a 꽃집 but no 은행.
On the map, the park has only a 카페.
You used the clue that only one place has both a 편의점 and a 은행.

stages.after: On the map, only the 정문 has both a 편의점 and a 은행, so 정문 is the best answer so far.

stages.info:
[학교 알림] 지난달에 후문 앞에도 은행이 새로 생겼어요.
유나: 은행 옆에 꽃집도 보여요.
stages.ask: Now where do you think 유나 is?

options.reveals: You noticed that the new notice means 은행 no longer separates the gates and that 꽃집 does.
You kept your earlier answer. Check whether the 은행 clue is still unique after the new notice.
The park has only a 카페, and 유나 sees neither a 은행 nor a 카페.

stages.after: The new bank means 은행 is at both gates now. The 꽃집 is still only at the 후문, so 유나 is at the 후문.

steps.reflect: The 은행 clue was strong until a notice changed the facts; the 꽃집 clue stayed unique. A good guess depends on which clues still point to only one place.

steps.prompt: You are at the 정문 and 유나 is at the 후문. Write a short Korean message to 유나: say where you are and what you will do (or ask her to do).

checks.label: says what to do (go / come / wait)

selfAssess: Does 유나 know where I am?
Does she know who moves?
Is the message short and clear?

modelAnswers.text: 저는 정문 앞에 있어요. 지금 후문으로 갈게요.
modelAnswers.note: Says where you are and that you will move.

modelAnswers.text: 후문 앞에서 기다려 주세요. 제가 걸어서 갈게요!
modelAnswers.note: Asks her to wait and says you will come.

badAnswers.why: A question only; it neither says where you are nor what to do.
Casual, no gate named, no polite ending.

steps.humanReview: Whether the plan is clear (who moves where) and the Korean is natural.
hints: Name the gate where you stand.
Add one verb: 갈게요 (I will go), 기다려 주세요 (please wait) or 오세요 (please come).

rubric.full: Gives reasonable answers at each stage and changes the last one because of the notice
rubric.partial: Updates at the second stage but keeps the old answer at the third

rubric.full: Names a gate, says who moves, polite
rubric.partial: Names a gate or an action but not both
rubric.none: Neither a place nor an action

alternatives: At the first stage, guessing 정문 or 후문 is reasonable if the student knows it is only a guess.
hardCases: A student may say the new 은행 at the 후문 could mean the old 정문 clue was a mistake; it was not, it was true at that time.

cautions.language: 정문 = front gate, 후문 = back gate; 앞 here means 'in front of'; -에서 기다려 주세요 = please wait at ...
cautions.culture: Korean schools commonly have a front gate and a back gate with shops outside; the map states the facts so no local knowledge is needed.
cautions.accessibility: The map is a text list instead of an image; each stage is read as plain text.

auto: Reasonable answers at each stage; gate, action and polite ending in the message
human: Clarity and naturalness of the message

subject: korean
title: From notice to text to a friend
goal: Decide which facts of a school notice a classmate must receive, then rewrite them in a friendly casual message without losing a fact.
thinking: Selecting essential facts
Changing register for a new reader
Keeping facts while changing the style
differsFromPlain: Plain practice translates or copies a notice. Here you choose what the reader needs and rewrite it in a different register for a close classmate.
prerequisites: Can read Hangul and a short school notice
Knows that casual speech (반말) is used with close friends
material:
Your classmate 하준 was absent today. You want to send him a text about this notice from your teacher.

[알림] 내일은 비가 온다고 합니다. 3교시 체육 수업은 운동장이 아니라 강당에서 합니다. 실내화를 가져오세요.

steps.prompt: Which things MUST stay in your text to 하준? Choose all that apply.

options.reveals: A heading belongs to the notice's form, not to what the reader needs to do.

options.text: The place of the class (강당, not the field)
options.reveals: You kept the fact that changes where he has to go.
The ending belongs to the notice's style; a friend does not need it.
You kept the fact that tells him when the change matters.
You kept the fact that tells him what to do.

steps.explain: 하준 needs the place (강당), the period (3교시) and what to bring (실내화). The heading and the stiff endings belong to the form of the notice.
hints: Imagine 하준 tomorrow morning: what does he need to know to be in the right place with the right things?
Separate facts from the notice's style.

acceptable.reason: The three facts are the core.

steps.prompt: Write a text to 하준 in casual speech (반말) that keeps those facts. You may add the reason (it will rain).
selfAssess: Are all three facts in my text?
Does it sound like me writing to a classmate, not like a notice?
Is it short?

modelAnswers.text: 내일 비 온대. 3교시 체육은 강당에서 해! 실내화 챙겨 와.
modelAnswers.note: Keeps all facts and adds the reason.

modelAnswers.text: 하준아, 내일 3교시 체육 강당에서 한대. 실내화 가져와야 돼!
modelAnswers.note: Friendly, casual, all facts present.

badAnswers.text: 내일 3교시 체육은 강당에서 합니다. 실내화를 가져오세요.
badAnswers.why: All facts, but copies the stiff notice style.
Casual but loses the place, period and what to bring.

steps.humanReview: Whether the casual register is natural and no fact is changed.
hints: Write the three facts as three short pieces: when, where, what to bring.
End each piece with -어/아 or -대 instead of -ㅂ니다.

rubric.full: Chooses place, period and what to bring and leaves out form details
rubric.partial: Chooses two of the three facts

rubric.full: All three facts, casual register, natural
rubric.partial: Facts present but register is stiff

alternatives: Adding the reason (it will rain) is allowed and good.
A polite -요 ending is an acceptable register for a classmate you do not know well; the checks only reject notice-style -ㅂ니다.
hardCases: Whether 'bring 실내화 instead of 운동화' counts as an extra fact; it is not in the notice, so do not require it.

cautions.language: -대 / -ㄴ대 reports what someone said (비 온대 = they say it will rain); 반말 = casual speech, -어/아 endings without 요.
cautions.culture: Korean students switch from -ㅂ니다 style notices to casual speech with classmates; some groups of students use -요 even among friends.
cautions.accessibility: The notice is plain text, with no image or color. 3교시 is written with digits + 교시 so screen readers read it in Korean.

auto: Which facts are chosen; presence of 강당, 실내화, 3교시 and absence of -ㅂ니다 endings
human: Naturalness of the casual register, whether it fits the writer's relationship

subject: korean
title: Plan a Saturday
goal: Test which plan fits a center's timetable and a friend's wishes, then write your own short plan that fills the gaps in the day.
thinking: Checking a plan against two sources
Making choices in the free time
Writing an ordered plan
differsFromPlain: Plain practice asks for the time of one class. Here you must find a plan that satisfies a timetable and a wish together, and then write your own plan, deciding what to do in the free time.
prerequisites: Can read times written with 시 and 분
Knows to suggest an activity with -자 or -ㄹ까
material:
You and your friend 하은 want to spend Saturday at the neighborhood culture center. Read the center's notice and the message.

[문화센터 토요일 안내]
- 그림 교실: 오전 10시 ~ 11시 30분
- 문화센터 식당: 낮 12시 ~ 1시 (점심만)
- 요리 교실: 오후 2시 ~ 4시

하은: 토요일에 문화센터에서 같이 놀자! 나는 그림 교실이랑 요리 교실 둘 다 하고 싶어. 점심도 꼭 먹고 싶어.

steps.prompt: Which plan satisfies the notice AND what 하은 wants?

options.reveals: You matched each activity to its time on the notice.
Lunch at 4시 does not fit the times of the center's restaurant.
The 그림 교실 is not open at 1시; check when it runs.

steps.explain: Only the plan in b follows the notice: 그림 교실 10시 ~ 11시 30분, 점심 12시 ~ 1시 and 요리 교실 2시 ~ 4시.
hints: Put the three activities in order of their times on the notice.
Check each activity of a plan against its own line in the notice.

steps.prompt: Now write YOUR plan to 하은 in Korean. Use the order of the day, give at least three clock times, and add one thing of your own in a free gap (for example where to meet or what to do between the classes).

checks.label: mentions 그림 교실 before 요리 교실
gives at least three clock times

selfAssess: Does my order follow the notice?
Did I add something of my own in a free gap?
Would 하은 know where to go and when?

modelAnswers.text: 10시에 그림 교실에 가자. 11시 30분에 끝나면 12시에 식당에서 점심 먹자. 2시에 요리 교실 가자!
modelAnswers.note: Follows the notice; uses the gap before lunch.

modelAnswers.text: 9시 50분에 문화센터 앞에서 만나자. 10시 그림 교실, 12시 점심, 2시 요리 교실 순서로 하자. 1시에는 공원에서 쉬자.
modelAnswers.note: Adds a meeting time and a rest in the gap.

badAnswers.why: No times and no lunch.

badAnswers.text: 2시에 요리 교실, 3시에 그림 교실, 4시에 점심 먹자.
badAnswers.why: Order and times do not follow the notice.

steps.humanReview: Whether the plan is realistic (the free gaps are used sensibly) and the Korean is natural.
hints: Write the day in order, from morning to afternoon, with a clock time for each part.
Look for the free time between 11시 30분 and 12시, and between 1시 and 2시.

rubric.full: Order and times follow the notice and include lunch
rubric.partial: Mostly follows the notice but one time is off

rubric.full: Adds a sensible own choice in a free gap
rubric.partial: Plan only repeats the notice

alternatives: Moving lunch to 12시 30분 is valid because the restaurant is open from 12시 to 1시.
A plan that skips the gap activity but is correct otherwise still passes the main checks.
hardCases: Meeting at 9시 50분 is not in the notice but is a reasonable own addition; a teacher decides whether it fits the friends' routine.

cautions.language: Suggestions to a friend use -자 (let's) or -ㄹ까?; ~에 means 'at (a time)'. 점심 = lunch, 식당 = restaurant.
cautions.culture: Neighborhood culture centers with art and cooking classes are common in Korea but the notice states all the facts.
cautions.accessibility: The timetable is a text list, with no table or color. Times are written with 시 and 분.

auto: Choice of the plan; presence of the activities, lunch, three clock times and their order
human: Whether the own addition is sensible and the Korean natural

subject: korean
title: A reply that contradicts the notice
goal: Check a draft reply against a notice, find the line that contradicts it, and fix the sentence.
thinking: Verifying each statement against a notice
Finding the conflicting detail
Repairing a sentence to fit the facts
differsFromPlain: Plain practice asks what a notice says. Here you check someone's own message against it and repair what does not fit.
prerequisites: Can read a short notice and a message in Korean
Knows -아요/어요 and -ㄹ게요 endings
material:
You are helping your younger cousin 소민 send a reply to her teacher. Read the notice and the draft.

[방학 과학 교실]
- 날짜: 7월 21일(월), 23일(수), 25일(금)
- 시간: 오전 9시 ~ 11시 30분
- 준비물: 물병, 필기도구 (실험 도구는 학교에서 준비해요)
- 점심 식사는 없어요.

선생님: 과학 교실에 오고 싶은 학생은 7월 18일까지 답장해 주세요.

steps.prompt: One line of the draft reply does not fit the notice. Which line is it?
lines: 안녕하세요, 선생님. 저는 과학 교실에 가고 싶어요.
steps.explain: Line 3 is wrong: the notice says 점심 식사는 없어요, so there is no school lunch. The other lines match the notice (days, start time and things to bring).
hints: Read the notice and mark one detail for each line of the draft.
Look for a line that says something the notice denies.

steps.prompt: Rewrite line 3 so that it fits the notice. Keep polite speech (-요) like the other lines.

checks.label: says lunch is eaten at home or brought (not school lunch)

selfAssess: Does my sentence agree with the notice (no school lunch)?
Did I say what I will do about lunch?
Is the Korean polite and natural?

modelAnswers.text: 점심은 집에서 먹고 올게요.
modelAnswers.note: Fixes the plan by eating before coming.

modelAnswers.text: 수업이 11시 30분에 끝나요. 점심은 도시락을 싸 갈게요.
modelAnswers.note: Keeps the time fact and brings a packed lunch.

badAnswers.why: Repeats the contradiction.
Mentions lunch but gives no plan.

steps.humanReview: Whether the fixed sentence is natural and consistent with the notice (for example, 11시 30분 end time).
hints: Find what the notice says about 점심.
Say what you will do instead: eat somewhere else or bring something.

rubric.full: Picks the line that contradicts the notice
rubric.partial: Picks a line that matches

rubric.full: Lunch plan that fits the notice, polite and natural
rubric.partial: Fits the notice but is not polite or is unclear

alternatives: Going home for lunch or bringing a packed lunch are both acceptable fixes.
Leaving 11시 30분 in the fixed sentence is fine.
hardCases: Line 2 uses the ending -지요, which asks for confirmation; it matches the notice and is not an error.

cautions.language: -지요? asks for agreement ('right?'); 급식 = school meals (not in this notice); 도시락 = packed lunch.
cautions.culture: Korean schools often serve lunch (급식), so a student might expect one; here the notice says there is none.
cautions.accessibility: The notice is a plain list. Dates are written as digits + 월/일 and weekdays in brackets.

auto: Which line is picked; polite ending, 점심 and a plan for lunch in the fix
human: Naturalness and consistency of the fixed line

subject: korean
title: Will the bus stop for 소라?
goal: Decide whether a friend's travel plan works by combining a bus notice with what day tomorrow is, and write a helpful reply.
thinking: Combining a rule with the date
Rejecting a tempting but irrelevant rule
Explaining the reason to a friend
differsFromPlain: Plain practice asks when a bus comes. Here a weekend timetable looks as if it solves the case, but a different rule decides, and you must find it.
prerequisites: Can read Hangul and times written with 시
Knows weekday names and polite -요 endings
material:
Today is 토요일. You are waiting at the bus stop and read the notice. Your friend 소라 will visit you tomorrow.

[마을버스 7번 안내]
- 첫차 6시, 막차 밤 9시 30분
- 평일: 15분마다 / 주말: 30분마다
- 일요일에는 도서관 앞 정류장에 서지 않아요.

소라: 내일 도서관 앞 정류장에서 7번 버스를 탈게요. 3시쯤 도착해요!

steps.prompt: Will 소라's plan work tomorrow?

options.text: Yes. The bus runs from 6:00 to 9:30, and 3시 is in between.
options.reveals: You checked the hours of service but not the stop rule.

options.text: No. Tomorrow is Sunday, and 7번 does not stop there.
options.reveals: You combined the date with the rule about the stop.

options.text: Yes, but on weekends she may wait up to 30 minutes for the bus.
options.reveals: You used the weekend timetable, which is about how often the bus comes, not where it stops.

options.text: Cannot tell: the notice does not say which stop she should use.
options.reveals: The notice does name a stop, in the rule about Sunday.

steps.explain: Today is 토요일, so tomorrow is 일요일. The notice says 7번 does not stop at 도서관 앞 on Sundays. The hours and the weekend timetable do not change that.
hints: First find out which day of the week tomorrow is.
Search the notice for every line that mentions that day.

steps.prompt: Write a polite reply (-요) to 소라. Tell her that her plan does not work, give the reason, and suggest what she can do.

checks.label: says it will not stop or suggests another way

selfAssess: Do I say that the plan does not work, and why?
Do I give her something she can do?
Is the reply polite?

modelAnswers.text: 소라 씨, 일요일에는 7번이 도서관 앞에 서지 않아요. 다른 정류장에서 타세요.
modelAnswers.note: States the rule and a way out.

modelAnswers.text: 내일은 일요일이라서 도서관 앞 정류장에는 버스가 안 서요. 걸어서 오세요.
modelAnswers.note: Explains the day and suggests walking.

badAnswers.why: Does not mention the problem or the day.
Mentions the day but gives no information about the bus.

steps.humanReview: Whether the suggestion is realistic and natural.
hints: Start by naming the day and the stop.
Add one thing she can do instead, with a verb ending in -세요.

rubric.full: Combines the date with the stop rule and rejects the plan
rubric.partial: Reaches the right answer without naming the rule

rubric.full: Names the day, the problem and an alternative in polite Korean
rubric.partial: Says the plan fails without a reason or alternative

alternatives: Suggesting a different stop (for example 시청 앞) is fine even though the notice does not name one, as long as it is flagged as a suggestion.
hardCases: A student may say that 3시 on a Sunday may be fine if she takes another route; the plan as stated (library stop) still fails.

cautions.language: 서다 = (a vehicle) stops; 서지 않아요 = does not stop; 마다 = every; 일요일에는 stresses 'on Sundays'.
cautions.culture: Village buses in Korea can have special weekend rules; the notice explains them.
cautions.accessibility: The notice is a plain list, times are written with 시. No timetable image.

auto: Choice of the verdict; presence of 일요일, bus/stop and a negation or alternative in the reply
human: Whether the suggested alternative is realistic and natural

subject: korean
title: The message that changed, then changed back
goal: Track when a friend will arrive at a party as schedule messages change, and send a helpful message based on the final facts.
thinking: Updating a prediction after new information
Recognizing when a correction cancels an earlier message
Sending an accurate update
differsFromPlain: Plain practice calculates one arrival time. Here the facts change twice, the second change cancels the first, and your judgement must follow the latest facts.
prerequisites: Can read clock times written with 시 and 분
Can read a short message about a schedule
material: 하린 goes to English class on Wednesday and then walks 10 minutes to her friend 소미's birthday party at 4시. 하린 wants to know when she will arrive.

steps.prompt: Decide when 하린 will probably arrive after each new message.
hints: Find the time class ends in the latest message, then add the walk.
Check whether a newer message replaces an older one.

stages.ask: When will 하린 probably arrive at 소미's house?

options.reveals: That would be right if the class ended at 3시 30분.
You added the 10-minute walk to the end of the class.
That is longer than class end plus the walk.

stages.after: Class ends at 4시, and the walk takes 10 minutes, so about 4시 10분. She will be 10 minutes late.

stages.info: 학원 문자: 이번 주 수요일은 시험이라 수업이 3시 30분에 끝나요.
stages.ask: When will 하린 probably arrive now?

options.reveals: You kept the first answer. Check the new end time of the class.
That is later than both the old and the new class end plus the walk.
You used the new end time (3시 30분) and added the walk.

stages.after: The newest message says class ends at 3시 30분, so 하린 arrives about 3시 40분, before the party.

stages.info: 학원 문자: 죄송합니다. 앞의 문자를 잘못 보냈어요. 시험은 다음 주예요. 이번 주는 평소와 같아요.
stages.ask: When will 하린 probably arrive now?

options.reveals: You noticed that the correction cancels the exam message and the normal timetable applies.
You kept the exam message. Check what the correction says about this week.
That is too late even for the normal class plus the walk.

stages.after: The correction cancels the exam message, so the normal class (to 4시) applies and 하린 arrives about 4시 10분.

steps.reflect: Your answer moved away from the first message and then came back. The latest message about the same thing is the one to trust, and a correction can cancel an earlier change.

steps.prompt: Write a short message from 하린 to 소미 in Korean: say that she will be a little late and when she will arrive.
selfAssess: Does the message say she will be late?
Does it give a time that matches the final facts?
Is the tone friendly?

modelAnswers.text: 소미야, 미안해! 학원이 4시에 끝나서 10분쯤 늦을 것 같아.
modelAnswers.note: Gives the reason and the delay.

modelAnswers.text: 조금 늦어요. 4시 10분쯤 도착해요.
modelAnswers.note: Short and polite; gives the time.

badAnswers.why: No lateness and no time.
Does not answer the question.

steps.humanReview: Whether the time matches the final message (about 4시 10분).
hints: Say you will be late, then add the time or the number of minutes.
Add 미안해 or 조금 to make it friendly.

rubric.full: Follows each newest message and returns to the first answer after the correction
rubric.partial: Updates once but misses that the correction cancels the change

rubric.full: Says she will be late and when, in friendly Korean
rubric.partial: Gives a time without saying late, or the reverse

alternatives: At stage 3 an answer such as '4시 10분쯤' is the only one that follows the correction; at stages 1 and 2 only one answer is reasonable.
hardCases: A student who reads the walk as 10 minutes before the party may compute a different time; the material says the walk is after class.

cautions.language: 늦다 = to be late (늦을 것 같아 = I think I will be late); 앞의 문자 = the earlier message; 평소와 같아요 = it is as usual.
cautions.culture: Birthday parties after cram school (학원) are common; no special knowledge is required.
cautions.accessibility: All times are written with 시 and 분, and the stages are plain text.

auto: Whether the stage answers are reasonable; presence of lateness, a time and a soft tone in the message
